questions.question: The fine for extinguishing public lamps may extend to ______ as per Section 141 of The Electricity Act, 2003.
questions.solution:
Under Section 141 of the Electricity Act, 2003, the penalty for extinguishing public lamps without permission can extend to ₹2,000.
  • Context: This section deals with penalties for damaging or interfering with public street lighting infrastructure.
  • Objective: It ensures the maintenance of public safety and utility services by deterring vandalism.

questions.question: The First Amendment Act of the Constitution of India came up in ______.
questions.solution:
The First Amendment Act of the Constitution of India was enacted in 1951.
  • Purpose: It was introduced to overcome judicial hurdles in implementing Zamindari abolition laws and to place reasonable restrictions on the Right to Freedom of Speech.
  • Key Addition: It added the Ninth Schedule to protect specific laws from judicial review.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prohibits anyone from employing children below the age of fourteen in factories, mines, etc?
questions.solution:
Article 24 of the Indian Constitution is a Fundamental Right that prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in any factory, mine, or other hazardous occupations.
  • Concept: This falls under the Right against Exploitation.
  • Related Law: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, further details the enforcement of this constitutional provision.

questions.question: The 40th Amendment Act of 1976 was applied to which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The 40th Amendment Act, 1976 substituted Article 297 of the Constitution.
  • Scope: It specified that all lands, minerals, and other things of value underlying the ocean within the territorial waters, continental shelf, or the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of India shall vest in the Union.
  • Limits: It empowered Parliament to specify the limits of these maritime zones from time to time.

questions.question: Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar was the chairman of the ______ of the Constituent Assembly of India.
questions.solution:
Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar served as the Chairman of the Credentials Committee of the Constituent Assembly.
  • Role: He was also a crucial member of the Drafting Committee.
  • Contribution: He played a major role in drafting the provisions related to the judiciary and citizenship.

questions.question: Right to Information Act ______ mandates timely response to citizen requests for government information.
questions.solution:
The Right to Information (RTI) Act was passed in 2005.
  • Requirement: It mandates that government authorities must provide information requested by citizens within 30 days.
  • Purpose: It aims to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority.

questions.question: Which of the following words does NOT precede the word ‘Republic’ in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The word 'Federal' does not appear in the Preamble of the Constitution of India.
  • Preamble Text: India is described as a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.'
  • Note: While India is federal in structure, the Constitution refers to India as a 'Union of States' in Article 1.

questions.question: In India, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, ______ is a comprehensive law to provide for the protection of children from the offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography, while safeguarding the interests of the child.
questions.solution:
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was enacted in 2012.
  • Comprehensive Protection: It provides a legal framework to protect children from sexual assault, harassment, and pornography.
  • Child-Centric: The law is designed to be child-friendly, ensuring that the child's identity is protected throughout the legal process.

questions.question: The 74th Amendment Act of 1992 added a new Part______ to the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 inserted Part IX-A into the Constitution, titled 'The Municipalities'.
  • Articles: It covers Articles 243-P to 243-ZG.
  • Schedule: It also added the Twelfth Schedule, which lists 18 functional items for urban local bodies.

questions.question: The Constituent Assembly was recognised by Section ______ of the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
questions.solution:
The Constituent Assembly was recognized as a sovereign body by Section 8(1) of the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
  • Legislative Power: This section empowered the Assembly to make laws for the Dominion of India and to draft its future Constitution.
  • Freedom: It effectively ended the British Parliament's authority over the Indian legislature.

questions.question: Article ______ of the Indian Constitution states that ‘there shall be a Commission for the socially and educationally backward classes to be known as the National Commission for Backward Classes’.
questions.solution:
Article 338B (1) was inserted by the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 to establish the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).
  • Mandate: It serves as a constitutional body to safeguard the interests of socially and educationally backward classes.
  • Functions: The commission investigates complaints and welfare measures for these classes.

questions.question: The ______ Amendment Act of the Constitution of India introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India.
questions.solution:
The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India.
  • Effective Date: It came into effect on July 1, 2017.
  • Impact: It replaced multiple indirect taxes levied by the Centre and States (like VAT and Excise Duty) with a single comprehensive tax.

questions.question: GV Mavalankar was the Chairman of the ______ of the Constituent Assembly of India.
questions.option_2: Ad hoc Committee on the National Flag
questions.option_4: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas
questions.solution:
G.V. Mavalankar was the Chairman of the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly.
  • First Speaker: He later became the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament).
  • Legacy: Known as the 'Father of the Lok Sabha', he played a vital role in establishing parliamentary procedures.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the right to equality?
questions.solution:
Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution of India deal with the Right to Equality.
  • Article 14: Equality before law and equal protection of laws.
  • Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability.
  • Article 18: Abolition of Titles (except military and academic).

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts of the Constitution of India abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely states?
questions.solution:
The 26th Amendment Act, 1971 abolished the Privy Purses and privileges of the former rulers of princely states.
  • Context: Privy Purses were annual payments made to rulers as part of the integration of their states into India.
  • Equality: The amendment aimed to remove the unconstitutional privileges of hereditary rulers in a democratic republic.

questions.question: An amendment to the Right to Information Act 2005 proposing that the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners be appointed ‘for such term as may be prescribed by the Central Government’ was passed in the year _____.
questions.solution:
The Right to Information (Amendment) Act, which gave the Central Government power to set the tenure and salaries of Information Commissioners, was passed in 2019.
  • Previous Rule: Before this, the tenure was fixed at 5 years.
  • Controversy: Critics argued this amendment could undermine the independence of the RTI watchdog.

questions.question: With reference to no-confidence motion, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: It is moved for ascertaining the confidence of Lok Sabha in the council of ministers.
questions.option_2: If it is passed in the Lok Sabha, the council of ministers must resign from office.
questions.option_3: It can be moved against the entire council of ministers only.
questions.option_4: It should state the reasons for its adoption in the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is that a No-Confidence Motion 'should state the reasons for its adoption'.
  • Rule: In the Lok Sabha, a No-Confidence Motion does not need to state the reasons for its introduction.
  • Requirement: It needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted for discussion.

questions.question: The salary and allowances of leaders of opposition in parliament are governed by the Act passed for the first time by the parliament in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act was passed for the first time in 1977.
  • Statutory Status: This act gave the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) the same status and perks as a Cabinet Minister.
  • Role: The LoP is the leader of the largest opposition party having at least one-tenth of the total seats in the House.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India amended Article 19 and inserted provisions fully securing the constitutional validity of zamindari abolition laws in general and certain specified State Acts in particular?
questions.solution:
The First Amendment Act, 1951 amended Article 19 and introduced provisions to protect Zamindari abolition laws.
  • Constitutional Validity: It inserted Articles 31A and 31B to ensure that land reform laws could not be challenged in court for violating Fundamental Rights.
  • Schedule: This amendment created the Ninth Schedule.

questions.question: When was the Tenth Session of the Constituent Assembly held?
questions.solution:
The Tenth Session of the Constituent Assembly was held from October 6 to October 17, 1949.
  • Context: During this session, the Assembly focused on completing the second reading of the draft Constitution.
  • Final Sessions: There were 11 total sessions; the final session was held in November 1949.

questions.question: Which amendment to the Constitution of India added a new subject in the Union List called 'taxes on services’?
questions.solution:
The 88th Amendment Act, 2003 added a new subject called 'Taxes on Services' to the Union List.
  • New Article: It inserted Article 268-A regarding service tax.
  • Purpose: It provided a legal framework for the Union to levy service tax and for its collection and appropriation by the Union and States.

questions.question: The _____ considers a marriage as complete and binding at the completion of the Saptapadi ritual.
questions.solution:
The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 considers a marriage complete and binding upon the performance of the Saptapadi (taking seven steps around the sacred fire).
  • Validity: According to Section 7, the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.
  • Coverage: This act applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs.

questions.question: Who among the following became a part of the Constituent Assembly from Madras Constituency in 1946?
questions.solution:
Ammu Swaminathan was a member of the Constituent Assembly from the Madras Constituency.
  • Background: She was a prominent social reformer and politician who advocated for the rights of women and the Dalit community.
  • Family: She was the mother of Dr. Lakshmi Sahgal, who led the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India was enacted in 1993 to constitutionally recognise municipal governments?
questions.solution:
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (enacted in 1993) provides constitutional recognition to Municipal Governments (Urban Local Bodies).
  • Tiers: It established three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations.
  • Note: The 73rd Amendment did the same for rural bodies (Panchayats).

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India were borrowed from the ______ Constitution.
questions.solution:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
  • Placement: DPSP are contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Indian Constitution.
  • Nature: These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law, but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following decades was proclaimed by the General Assembly of the United Nations as the International Decade for action on ‘Water for life’?
questions.solution:
The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed the period 2005 - 2015 as the 'Water for Life' International Decade for Action.
  • Goal: The primary goal was to promote efforts to fulfill international commitments made on water and water-related issues.
  • Significance: It aimed to ensure the sustainable management of freshwater resources globally.

questions.question: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955 as part of the Hindu Code Bills.
  • Reform: It brought about significant changes, such as prohibiting polygamy and introducing provisions for divorce.
  • Applicability: It governs the matrimonial laws for Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and Buddhists.

questions.question: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution of India ______.
questions.option_1: reduced the age for voting from 21 to 18 years
questions.option_3: restricted the size of council of ministers to 15% of the number of legislative members
questions.option_4: exempted Arunachal Pradesh from reservation for Scheduled Castes in Panchayati Raj institutions
questions.solution:
The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years.
  • Article Amended: It amended Article 326 of the Constitution.
  • Reason: The change was made to increase the participation of the youth in the democratic process of the country.

questions.question: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was consisted of ______ members.
questions.solution:
The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly consisted of 7 members.
  • Chairman: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman of this committee.
  • Members: Other members included N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, Dr. K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau, and T.T. Krishnamachari.

questions.question: Realising the importance of maintaining the cleanliness of the water bodies, the Government of India passed the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, ________, to safeguard our water resources.
questions.solution:
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed in 1974.
  • Establishment: It led to the creation of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards.
  • Objective: To maintain and restore the wholesomeness of water and to prevent water pollution in India.
